name: supabase
description: Supabase (Postgres) on one production database: RLS and grant rules, guard overlay, post-merge migration apply with a live privilege assertion, and a CI grant checker.

facts.name: DB_PROJECT_REF
facts.meaning: The one Supabase project ref. There is no QA project.
facts.ask: What is the Supabase project ref (the id in the project URL)? It is not a secret.

facts.name: MIGRATION_TOOL
facts.meaning: How schema changes are applied: supabase-cli or mcp-apply. Default supabase-cli when supabase/migrations/ exists.
facts.ask: How should schema changes be applied? (1) supabase-cli: migration files live in the repo; an additive one is applied with `supabase db push` before merge, once /guard passes. Pro: every migration is in the PR diff, so review and the CI grant checker see it. Con: needs the Supabase CLI and the database password on the machine that applies, and a file edited in the wrong checkout is a trap. (2) mcp-apply: the agent applies SQL with the Supabase MCP `apply_migration` tool and the migration ledger is the record. Pro: no CLI setup and no folder that can drift from the ledger. Con: the SQL is not in the repo, so CI can't check it and reviewers only see it in the PR description; it needs a second, write-enabled MCP server.

facts.name: MIGRATIONS_DIR
facts.meaning: Where migration files live. `none` with mcp-apply.
facts.ask: Where do migration files live? (Default supabase/migrations; `none` with mcp-apply.)

facts.name: RLS_HELPER_EXEMPTIONS
facts.meaning: RLS helper functions that policies call as the requesting role, kept executable by anon/authenticated, as schema.name(arg types). Default none.
facts.ask: Do any RLS policies call a helper function as the requesting user (so it must stay executable by anon/authenticated)? List each as schema.name(argument types), or answer none (the default).

owner_tasks.task: With MIGRATION_TOOL supabase-cli: install the Supabase CLI and link this repo to the project (supabase link --project-ref with the DB_PROJECT_REF value)
owner_tasks.why: the /verify apply step runs supabase db push --dry-run and supabase db push from the branch checkout

owner_tasks.task: Add a second, write-enabled Supabase MCP server named supabase_apply to .mcp.json (the supabase entry's URL without read_only=true) and never pre-allow its tools
owner_tasks.why: with MIGRATION_TOOL mcp-apply, migrations are applied with its apply_migration tool, and every call should prompt

env.name: SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN
env.purpose: Access token for the Supabase MCP server and the Supabase CLI.
env.how_to_get: Owner task: Supabase dashboard > Account > Access Tokens > Generate new token. Put it in your shell environment or secret manager, never in a committed file.

env.name: SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD
env.purpose: Only with MIGRATION_TOOL supabase-cli: lets `supabase db push` reach the database when a guarded migration is applied.
env.how_to_get: Owner task: Supabase dashboard > Project Settings > Database (reset it there if unknown). Keep it in your shell environment or secret manager.
